routeSelection.basis: The generic Computing Science target does not identify a track. The current adopted OER lists Cyber Security, Software Science and Data Science as three equally formal 12-EC options without designating a general track. Its first-listed track is selected as a neutral tie-break, not for UCR fit.

audience.programmeDescription: Computing Science studies how software and computing systems are designed, implemented and analysed. Radboud combines programming, algorithms, mathematical foundations, information systems and security with independent research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The adopted curriculum allocates 180 EC, but entry and participation conditions for three newly compulsory courses remain unverified. Relevant UCR computing, mathematics, data and AI study has been assessed provisionally. A final comparison is withheld until those external conditions can be checked.

curriculum.routeLabel: Cyber Security track; entry verification pending
curriculum.limitation: The adopted allocation totals 180 EC: 129 EC core, a 12-EC Cyber Security track, a 15-EC minor, 12 EC of open electives and a 12-EC thesis. This is not yet a fully verified pathway. Entry and participation conditions for AI-Assisted Development, Human-Computer Interaction and Information Retrieval remain unverified. The language assessment requires participation, not a passing result; writing skills are integrated into existing credits.

componentNotes.thesis: Required 12 EC individual research thesis, approved in advance. Entry: at least 120 programme EC including the complete first year. Research Methods is recommended, not an additional hard condition.
componentNotes.minor: One approved coherent 15 EC minor. The regulations exclude several overlapping Computing Science minors; a separately composed minor needs examination-board approval.
